questions.question: Explain the difference between kth smallest element and successor and predecessor in BST.
questions.ideal_answer: kth smallest element and successor and predecessor differ in several ways: kth smallest element is order statistic query (works by O(h) with augmented size, O(n) naive) whereas successor and predecessor is inorder neighbors (works by next larger / next smaller element). kth smallest element is typically used for left subtree size determines position, while successor and predecessor is used for successor: right subtree min, or nearest ancestor where node is in left subtree. Example demonstrating kth smallest element: int leftSize = size(root.left); if (k <= leftSize) return kthSmallest(root.left, k); else if (k == leftSize + 1) return root.val; else return kthSmallest(root.right, k - leftSize - 1);. Example demonstrating successor and predecessor: Node succ = null; while (root != null) { if (p.val < root.val) { succ = root; root = root.left; } else root = root.right; }.

questions.question: What is BST deletion in BST and how does it work?
questions.ideal_answer: BST deletion in BST refers to node removal with structure preservation. It works by 0, 1, or 2 child cases. Key characteristics include leaf: remove; one child: replace; two children: replace with inorder successor/predecessor. Example: if (root.left == null) return root.right; if (root.right == null) return root.left; Node min = findMin(root.right); root.val = min.val; root.right = delete(root.right, min.val);. Common pitfalls include Hibbard deletion asymmetry.
